pairs.evidence: app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/Document.tsx:198 The render gate's escape hatch names only a version, so one click waives every blocking finding on that staged version and no single finding can be accepted while the others keep blocking, which the technique's two-findings test defines as a blanket.

techniques.evidence: app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/Document.tsx:198 The op carries versionId and no rule or site. The receipt (lib/script/versions.ts GateOverride) records which renders blocked, after the fact and at render granularity. Low blast radius: one operator, one version, and the blocking list is drawn beside the button.

app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/Document.tsx:258 The skip is rendered and counted beside violations, and the enforced percentage sits next to it, so a pass with holes does not read as a full pass.

app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/Document.tsx:161 An accepted version keeps its override visible in the history. The hole is written by the same act that advances it (fixtureScript.ts accept-over-gate), and the per-kind module is shared with the real side.
app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/Findings.tsx:5 One findings renderer with a closed verdict vocabulary serves both checks, so the two surfaces cannot diverge on what a verdict means.

app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/Document.tsx:197 A blocked gate removes the plain accept action and leaves only the recorded override. The server half also refuses `accept` on a blocked gate (fixtureScript.ts:181).

pairs.registryProposal: waiver-names-its-finding and advancement-evidence-fields pull apart on a human-judgment override of a lexical gate: the second endorses advancing the whole item with the hole recorded, the first calls any waiver that cannot name a single finding a blanket. The standard could say whether a per-item override with a frozen receipt of its findings is a third permitted shape or still a blanket.
